statement: Dana makes and sells candles. Each month her supplies cost $150$ dollars plus $2.40$ dollars per candle, and she sells each candle for $9$ dollars. What is the least number of candles she must make and sell in a month to earn a profit of at least $600$ dollars?

choices.misconception: I left out the 2.40-dollar cost of each candle and solved $9n - 150 \ge 600$, which gave about 83.3, so I said 84.
I left out the 150-dollar fixed cost and solved $6.60n \ge 600$, which gave about 90.9, so I said 91.
I solved $6.60n \ge 750$ to get about 113.6 and rounded down to 113, but 113 candles give a profit of only 595.80 dollars.

hints: Profit is money in minus all of the money out.
Write the profit for $n$ candles as $9n - (150 + 2.40n)$, set it greater than or equal to $600$, and solve. The answer must be a whole number.

solutions.reliable: For $n$ candles, revenue is $9n$ and cost is $150 + 2.40n$, so profit is $6.60n - 150$. Solve $6.60n - 150 \ge 600$: $6.60n \ge 750$ and $n \ge 113.64$. The least whole number is $114$. Check: $6.60(114) - 150 = 602.40 \ge 600$, but $6.60(113) - 150 = 595.80$. Key idea: build profit as revenue minus every cost, then round up when the question asks for a minimum.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
